extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners and patent practitioners preparing or reviewing affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 and 1.132
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, presenting, and evaluating affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 (antedating references) and 1.132 (traversing rejections), including required content, acceptable evidence, timeliness, examiner responsibilities, and common reasons for insufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declarant statement of truth and belief
rubrics_metrics.description: The declarant must set forth in the body of the declaration that all statements made of the declarant’s own knowledge are true and that all statements made on information and belief are believed to be true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit/declaration must include explicit wording attesting truthfulness of statements of own knowledge and belief; false statements may violate 18 U.S.C. 1001 and jeopardize validity of application or patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling references that claim the same invention
rubrics_metrics.description: When the reference is a noncommonly owned U.S. patent or patent application publication claiming the same invention and its publication date is less than 1 year prior to presentation of claims, applicant’s remedy, if any, must be by way of 37 CFR 41.202 instead of 37 CFR 1.131; such references can be overcome only by interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a U.S. patent claims same invention and issue date is more than 1 year prior to presentation of claims, rejection under 35 U.S.C. 135(b)(1) should be made; for application publications, 35 U.S.C. 135(b)(2) applies only if the application being examined was filed after the publication date. Note these facts in the Office action. See MPEP Chapter 2300 and In re McGrew.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on using 37 CFR 1.131 to avoid interference
rubrics_metrics.description: A 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit is ineffective to overcome a U.S. patent or application publication that claims applicant’s invention when the claims are identical or not patentably distinct such that an interference would exist under 37 CFR 41.203(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where commonly owned claims are not patentably distinct, terminal disclaimer and 37 CFR 1.130 may overcome a 103 rejection; but 1.131 cannot be used to avoid creation of two patents on the same invention. See case law (In re Clark, In re Hidy, In re Teague, etc.) and MPEP § 718. Form paragraph 7.58 may be used to note such situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits/declarations must allege FACTS not conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: The essential thing to be shown under 37 CFR 1.131 is priority of invention by satisfactory evidence of FACTS; FACTS, not conclusions, must be alleged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A general allegation that the invention was completed prior to the reference is insufficient. Declarations that merely state conclusions (e.g., 'invention was conceived prior to X') without factual details are inadequate. See Ex parte Saunders, In re Borkowski, In re Harry for examples of insufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable documentary exhibits and how to refer to them
rubrics_metrics.description: Each exhibit relied upon should be specifically referred to in the affidavit or declaration in terms of what it is relied upon to show. Examples of acceptable exhibits include attached sketches, blueprints, photographs, reproductions of notebook entries, an accompanying model, supporting witness statements, testimony given in an interference, and disclosure documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List (A)-(H) in MPEP § 715.07 illustrate common exhibits. When relying on interference testimony, point out which parts are relied on—examiners will not search entire records. Exhibits and models must comply with 37 CFR 1.91 to be entered into the application file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original exhibits or satisfactory explanation for absence
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.131(b) requires that original exhibits of drawings or records, or photocopies thereof, accompany and form part of the affidavit or declaration or that their absence be satisfactorily explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If originals were lost, reproduce and furnish them or explain loss. If disclosure was by verbal disclosure only, witnesses should state as nearly as possible the language used. See Ex parte Donovan and related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibits need not support all claim limitations if declaration supplies missing parts
rubrics_metrics.description: An accompanying exhibit need not support all claimed limitations, provided that any missing limitation is supported by the declaration itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must consider the affidavit/declaration and all accompanying exhibits, records and notes in their entirety when reviewing sufficiency. See Ex parte Ovshinsky.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of exhibits and specificity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must give a clear explanation of the exhibits, pointing out exactly what facts are established and relied on; vague, general statements about what exhibits describe are insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements that exhibits 'amount to mere pleading, unsupported by proof or a showing of facts' do not satisfy 37 CFR 1.131(b). See In re Borkowski and In re Harry; provide explicit explanation of what each exhibit proves and when events occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing dates: actual dates vs. specified-date allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: When alleging conception or reduction to practice prior to the effective date of the reference, dates in the oath or declaration may be actual dates or may allege that acts occurred prior to a specified date; however, actual dates of acts relied on to establish diligence must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If dates on exhibits were removed, explain dates in the oath/declaration. MPEP § 715.07(a) discusses the diligence requirement tied to actual dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three acceptable ways to show prior invention under 37 CFR 1.131
rubrics_metrics.description: (A) Actual reduction to practice prior to the effective date of the reference; (B) Conception prior to the effective date coupled with due diligence from prior to the reference date to a subsequent actual reduction to practice; or (C) Conception prior to the effective date coupled with due diligence from prior to the reference date to the filing date of the application (constructive reduction to practice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conception must be proven (drawings, disclosure, model, etc.). Conception alone confers no rights unless followed by reasonable diligence to a reduction to practice or filing. See Mergenthaler v. Scudder, Automatic Weighing Mach., In re Asahi/America for standards on reduction to practice and simplicity exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of reduction to practice and utility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof of actual reduction to practice generally requires showing the apparatus actually existed and worked for its intended purpose; proof of utility is required only if the reference discloses a utility and depends on facts whether test results are necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some devices are so simple that mere construction suffices to constitute reduction to practice. Photographs plus articles and technical reports may suffice. The ultimate issue: would one of ordinary skill be satisfied to a reasonable certainty that the subject matter possessed the alleged utility. See In re Asahi/America, In re Blake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligence requirement and critical period
rubrics_metrics.description: Where conception occurs prior to the reference date but reduction to practice afterward, applicant must show diligence from just prior to the effective date of the reference (the critical period) continuously up to the date of an actual or constructive reduction to practice (filing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diligence is binary (diligent or not); inactivity must be excused by explanation; only diligence before reduction to practice is material. The lapse of time after reduction to practice until filing is not relevant to 1.131 practice. See Christie v. Seybold, In re Nelson, Ex parte Merz and MPEP § 2138.06 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference testimony may be used to antedate a reference
rubrics_metrics.description: In place of a 1.131 affidavit, testimony of the applicant in an interference may sometimes be used to antedate a reference; the parts of testimony forming the basis of priority should be pointed out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners are not expected to search entire interference records—applicant must identify which testimony is relied upon. See Ex parte Bowyer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts relied upon must occur in U.S., NAFTA, or WTO member country
rubrics_metrics.description: The 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit/declaration must contain an allegation that the acts relied upon to establish the date were carried out in this country or in a NAFTA country or WTO member country, consistent with 35 U.S.C. 104.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dates for reliance in NAFTA/WTO countries are limited: may establish completion in NAFTA countries on or after Dec 8, 1993, and in WTO member countries (other than NAFTA) on or after Jan 1, 1996. Acts occurring prior to those effective dates may still be relied upon; but a date of completion may not be established before those effective dates for those countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of exhibits must comply with 37 CFR 1.91
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibits filed as part of an affidavit or declaration must comply with requirements of 37 CFR 1.91 to be entered into an application file; noncompliant exhibits will be disposed of or returned at Office discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 608.03(a) for exhibit handling procedures and formatting/entry requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary examiner responsibility for 1.131 sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: The question of sufficiency of affidavits or declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 should be reviewed and decided by a primary examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review of formal sufficiency/propriety is by petition under 37 CFR 1.181 answered by Technology Center Directors; review on the merits is by appeal to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences. Use form paragraphs (e.g., 7.59, 7.63) where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seasonable presentation (timeliness) rules for 1.131 evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 are timely if submitted: (A) prior to a final rejection; (B) before appeal in an application not having a final rejection; (C) after final rejection but before or on same date as filing an appeal upon showing good and sufficient reasons; or (D) after prosecution is closed if filed with a request for continued examination (RCE) or a CPA where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All admitted affidavits/declarations must be acknowledged and commented upon by the examiner in the next succeeding action. Timeliness refusals are reviewable by petition, not appeal, per cited cases (In re Deters, Ex parte Hale).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review for prior public use/on-sale and best mode when evaluating 1.131 evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must review affidavits/declarations and accompanying evidence to determine whether they show that the claimed invention was 'in public use' or 'on sale' in this country more than one year prior to the effective filing date (statutory bar under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)), and must consider whether reliance on embodiments not disclosed in the application raises a best mode issue under 35 U.S.C. 112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if an affidavit overcomes the cited reference, applicant's own prior public use or sale may still bar patentability. A best mode rejection should only be made if record, by preponderance of the evidence, establishes that the specification did not set forth the best mode. See MPEP § 2133.03 and § 2165.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.132: affidavits/declarations traversing rejections must be sworn and responsive
rubrics_metrics.description: When any claim is rejected or objected to, evidence submitted to traverse the rejection on a basis not otherwise provided for must be by oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.132; the primary examiner must personally review and decide whether such evidence is responsive and presents sufficient facts to overcome the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All traversing affidavits/declarations not falling under other specific rules are treated under 1.132. Use form paragraphs 7.65/7.66 and subparagraphs 7.66.01–7.66.05 to comment on sufficiency and to state reasons for insufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common reasons an affidavit/declaration under 1.132 is insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavit/declaration may be insufficient for reasons including: untimely; fails to set forth facts; facts presented are not germane to the rejection at issue; showing is not commensurate in scope with the claims; affiant has never seen the invention before; statements only assert that invention works as intended; refers only to the invention generally and not to individual claims; no evidence of long-felt need; or conclusion that rebuttal evidence fails to outweigh evidence of obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 7.66 and 7.66.01–7.66.05 enumerate these categories and require a detailed explanation of why the affidavit/declaration is insufficient rather than general conclusory statements. See MPEP § 716 for examples and examiner notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective (secondary) evidence of nonobviousness must be considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits/declarations, when timely presented, containing evidence of criticality or unexpected results, commercial success, long-felt but unsolved needs, failure of others, skepticism of experts, etc., must be considered by the examiner in determining obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative data in the specification intended to illustrate the claimed invention must be considered. The lack of objective evidence does not weigh in favor of obviousness. Corroboration is not required in 1.131 practice; whether test results are needed to prove utility depends on facts. Cite Graham v. John Deere, Stratoflex, In re Margolis, Miles Labs, and other cases for precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generally applicable criteria for evidence traversing rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence traversing rejections must meet general criteria: (A) Timeliness — must be timely or seasonably filed per the rules; (B) Consideration of evidence — when timely presented, evidence must be considered by the examiner and entered affidavits/declarations acknowledged and commented upon in the next action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where evidence is found sufficient to overcome the prima facie case, the examiner's comments should follow guidelines for statements of reasons for allowance (MPEP § 1302.14). Where insufficient, the examiner must explain the reasons (see categories in MPEP § 716). For affidavits filed after appeal, see 37 CFR 41.33(d) and MPEP §§ 1206, 1211.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner must provide detailed explanations when rejecting entered evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: If an entered affidavit or declaration is deemed insufficient to overcome a rejection, the examiner must set forth the reasons for insufficiency with specific explanations rather than general statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General statements like 'the declaration lacks technical validity' or 'the evidence is not commensurate with the scope of the claims' without supporting explanation are insufficient. Use the form paragraphs and include specific factual or legal defects (e.g., untimely, lacks facts, not commensurate in scope).
